title: Same Buyer or Independent Buyers for the Volume-Tier Discount (base)
scenario_text:
Blueriver Data publishes a volume-tier discount ladder for enterprise licenses: Tier 1 at $250k–$500k combined ARR (7% discount), Tier 2 at $500k–$1M (12%), Tier 3 at $1M–$2M (18%). The policy states: 'For the purpose of tier calculation, contracts held by legal entities under common majority ownership are combined into a single buyer of record, provided both contracts are within the same trailing twelve months and the affiliation is documented in the Blueriver Account Hierarchy.'

Two active opportunities are up for signature this quarter. Opportunity A is a new $475,000 ARR renewal from Kestrel Logistics. Opportunity B is a $875,000 ARR expansion from Merlin Analytics. The two accounts appear separately in Salesforce with distinct primary contacts and distinct billing addresses.

The Blueriver Account Hierarchy (an internal registry maintained by RevOps and sourced from Dun & Bradstreet plus manual overrides) shows Kestrel Logistics as a wholly owned subsidiary of Aster Holdings, and Merlin Analytics as a wholly owned subsidiary of Aster Holdings as of last quarter's refresh. Aster Holdings itself is not a Blueriver customer. Deal Desk asks which volume tier applies.
question: Under Blueriver's volume-tier discount policy, what tier should this combined engagement receive?
choices: Tier 3 (18% discount) — treat Kestrel and Merlin as one combined buyer at $1.35M ARR.
Tier 2 (12% discount) — apply each contract at its own $475k / $875k ARR to Tier 2 individually.
Tier 1 (7% discount) — the two contracts do not share a buyer of record for policy purposes.
No standard tier — route to CRO for a bespoke pricing exception because affiliation is unclear.
